title: Triviality of line bundles on special linear matrix schemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $n\geq1$. Put $A=k[x_{ij}:1\leq i,j\leq n]/(\det(x_{ij})-1)$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, where determinant and affine spectrum are [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Every invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)=0$, where $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ means isomorphism classes of invertible modules, with tensor product as its group operation. There is no restriction on the characteristic of $k$.

source.place: Proposition 20.30, printed p.417; the scheme product decomposition of 2.42, printed p.53.

proof.text: Write $P=k[x_{ij}]$, $d=\det(x_{ij})$, $A=P/(d-1)$ and $B=P[1/d]$. The $n^2$ variables identify $\operatorname{Spec}P$ with affine $n^2$-space. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b), its basic open $D(d)$ is affine and has ring $B$; thus identify $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with that open subscheme. Here [def-weil-ring-localization-away] supplies $d^{-1}\in B$. We will construct a retraction $r:G\to X$ of a morphism $j:X\to G$.

source.place: Tags 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (3), and 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; Milne Proposition 20.30.

proof.text: Let $\bar x_{ij}\in A$ denote the residue classes. Evaluation $P\to A$, $x_{ij}\mapsto\bar x_{ij}$, sends $d$ to $1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] extends it to $q:B\to A$, with $q(d^{-1})=1$. In $B$ put $y_{i1}=d^{-1}x_{i1}$ and $y_{ij}=x_{ij}$ for $j>1$. Every monomial of the Leibniz determinant contains exactly one entry from the first column, so [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] gives $\det(y_{ij})=d^{-1}d=1$. Evaluation $P\to B$ at the $y_{ij}$ exists by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and kills $d-1$. It therefore induces $s:A\to B$, $[f]\mapsto f(y_{ij})$: if $f-f'=(d-1)h$, their evaluations agree. This uses the quotient in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Now $q(s(\bar x_{ij}))=\bar x_{ij}$ for every $i,j$ and both maps fix $k$, so $q\circ s=\mathrm{id}_A$. By the contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $j=\operatorname{Spec}q$ and $r=\operatorname{Spec}s$ satisfy $r\circ j=\mathrm{id}_X$. This is the retraction implicit in Milne's map $(M,t)\mapsto M\operatorname{diag}(t,1,\ldots,1)$: its inverse divides the first column by $\det M$.

source.place: Proposition 20.30, printed p.417, and 2.42, printed p.53; explicit coordinate and pullback argument.

proof.text: Let $L$ be any invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module. Set $M=r^*L$ by [def-pc-module-pullback]. On each inverse image $r^{-1}(U)$ of an open trivialization $L|_U\cong\mathcal O_U$ from [def-sc-invertible-module], tensor pullback identifies $M$ with $\mathcal O_{r^{-1}(U)}$: multiplication $a\otimes b\mapsto a\,r^\sharp(b)$ has inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. These opens cover $G$, so $M$ is locally free of rank one (hence an invertible module). The same multiplication formula, without choosing $U$, identifies $j^*\mathcal O_G$ with $\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 0B8L, lemma-pullback-invertible; local rank-one tensor calculation written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-space-open-invertible-trivial] with the field $k$, dimension $n^2$, open $G=D(d)$ from Step 1 and invertible module $M$ from Step 3. Its statement gives an isomorphism $a:r^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_G$ without any restriction on $k$. Pulling back $a$ by $j$ preserves its inverse because pullback is a functor. By [def-pc-module-pullback] and $r\circ j=\mathrm{id}_X$, we have $L\cong\mathrm{id}_X^*L\cong j^*r^*L\xrightarrow{j^*a}j^*\mathcal O_G\cong\mathcal O_X$, the last map being Step 3's multiplication isomorphism. Thus every class in the Picard group as defined in the statement equals the identity class. For $n=1$, $A=k[x]/(x-1)\cong k$, $s(\bar x)=x/x=1$, and the same retraction works. All formulas hold in every characteristic.
